summary: PentestAI v1.6 — one-click 'Launch in distro' workflow fully verified. 11/11 new v1.6 backend tests pass (auth gate, all 4 distro builders, shell-quoting safety, empty-target default, unknown 404, filename slug, regression: distros list, root version 1.5.0). 26/26 v1.4/v1.5 regression still passing. Frontend ToolkitsPage shows 4 Launch buttons with proper data-testids and triggers .sh downloads with correct Content-Disposition filenames + toast. DistroRecommendation on scan results renders a Launch button per recommended distro and correctly passes target+scan_id query params (verified by network interception during Kodachi launch from a completed recon scan).
critical_code_review_comments: launch_service._shell_quote() is correct for ASCII single-quote escape, but the docstring claims 'only ASCII safe contexts pass through' — in practice high-bit chars are not sanitised. Since target is only ever interpolated into a single-quoted env-export it remains injection-safe, but a defensive .encode('ascii','ignore') would be more honest with the docstring.

launch_service._preamble() interpolates raw `target` and `scan_id` into bash COMMENTS (lines starting with '#'). A newline in target would break out of the comment block and inject arbitrary bash. Currently the FastAPI query string handling URL-decodes %0A into \n. Recommend stripping CR/LF from target/scan_id before interpolation, OR move the comment interpolation through _shell_quote as well.
routers/distros.py /launch endpoint does no rate limiting. The endpoint is cheap to compute (no DB/network) but an attacker can use it as a small bash-script fuzzer. Low priority.

LaunchDistroButton.js does no MIME-type validation on response — if backend ever returned JSON error, the blob would be saved as .sh with HTML/JSON content. Consider checking response.headers['content-type'].startswith('text/x-shellscript') before constructing blob.

Filename slug in launch_service._slug() truncates to 40 chars but does NOT URL-encode for the Content-Disposition header. Currently safe because all non-alnum chars become '-', but if logic ever changes, RFC 5987 encoding would be safer.
